ModMetaData.name: Resource Readout+
ModMetaData.author: Cruesoe
ModMetaData.description:
Replaces the resource list at the top left of the map with a tidy panel in the look of the UI Rethemed mods.
Resources are sorted into groups you recognize: essentials, food (meat and fish, vegetables, animal products, animal feed), meals, medicine, drugs (social, hard, medical, serums and catalysts), textiles, materials, manufactured goods, ammo (mortar shells and any mod ammo), items and waste. Each group can be folded and shows its total. Make your own groups and subgroups, and rename, reorder or nest any group. An organizer window lists every group and resource: drag resources into order, hide or show them one by one, and move them between groups. Look-alike items such as leathers, wools, stone blocks, fish and eggs are combined into one row that opens to show each kind. The simple list and the category tree from the base game are still there as options, in the same look.
Every row can show the item's name, and hovering it shows its description, how many you have in storage and elsewhere on the map, their value and how the count has changed. Click a row to jump to where it is stored, clicking again for the next stack. Drag rows to reorder them or move them into another group. Right-click a row to pin it to the top, set a minimum stock, see its history, count every one on the map rather than just what is in storage, combine or separate look-alikes, or hide it. Rows below their minimum turn red, with an optional alert listing everything running low. Small arrows show what has gone up or down over the last day, each tooltip charts the last few days, and falling resources say roughly when they will run out. A filter on the title bar (or a hotkey) shows only what is trending, falling, low or new, and rows can be sorted by how much they changed. Resources stored for the first time, or back in stock after running out, get a mark that clears itself after a while or when clicked. A search box filters the list. A cog on the panel switches the list and opens the settings, including a background opacity slider.
Needs UI Rethemed - Core. Safe to add to an existing save. Removing it leaves harmless one-time errors about its saved trend history and new-resource records when the save next loads.
